**Conversation Overview**

This conversation is a continuation of an ongoing long-form technical project called "The Method 1.6," a multi-volume academic work being built and maintained across numbered chat sessions. The session is designated chat 30, operating under BUILD-31 protocols with a structured handoff system (HANDOFF-31 → HANDOFF-32). The person issues rulings that govern the project, maintains a working register of findings and decisions, and expects Claude to execute a formal reading gate (§0) before any work begins, printing a certificate of verified measurements before touching any file.

The primary accomplishment this session was completing B7: the reordering of the Spectra Compendium's 596-row channel table (SPEC-06), collapsing 92 species runs into 70 contiguous runs via a stable merge keyed on element name and roman-numeral ionisation stage. The reorder was verified by multiset invariant before and after writing, and both named hazards (the He II note travelling with its rows, and the re-heading of the headerless continuation block) were confirmed on the pressed object. The session also repaired `coords.py` at four sites after discovering it had silently failed for an entire build when Ruling 49's heading-level promotion broke its literal `### ` section locators—now generalized to match headings at any level. A new ruling (Ruling 56) was received verbatim from the person, designating the Löwdin solution's original input as an external authority for verifying indexes being built, which introduced B13 as a new queue item and reversed a standing instruction to retire the BUILD-12 bundles.

Two significant methodological findings were recorded: SPEC-12 established that `pdftotext` dropped 51 rows (seven species, 8–11 rows each) from the PDF text layer while the `.docx` carried them correctly, undermining the reliability of absence-in-text-layer as evidence of absence on the page; and W-034 documented that the handoff's own Register line count (5,894) was one entry stale at writing, with the file actually measuring 5,896 lines. The session closed with HANDOFF-32 written and BUILD-31 packed, with B8–B12 explicitly named as not started. The person's mid-session message ("My apologies. Continue") indicated an interruption, after which Claude resumed the open diagnostic without requesting re-orientation. The project enforces strict gate protocols, ruling-based governance, external measurement over recitation, and a standing lesson added this session: any structural ruling (heading levels, part numbering, heading names) is a silent-breakage event for every instrument that locates by structure, requiring all gates to be re-run before the build is declared current.

**Tool Knowledge**

Google Drive large-file download requires reading from `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<tool_call_id>.json` for files over approximately 1 MB. The working decode pattern is: `d=json.load(open(p)); inner=json.loads(d[0]['text']); blob=base64.b64decode(inner['content'])`, followed by byte-length verification against the Drive `fileSize` field. The figures zip (`The_Method_1_6_figures_BUILD13.zip`, Drive ID `1q7pvnxMPILD9AVoH6XjymZHXX79YzITd`, 6,299,293 bytes) was fetched and verified this session against sha256 prefix `ee423b9c...` and md5 `78888f20...`. The `xxd` tool is confirmed absent from this environment; `od -An -tx1` is the reliable substitute for terminal byte inspection. `pdftotext -layout` is confirmed to silently drop table rows that are present in `word/document.xml`—absence in its output is not evidence of absence on the rendered page, and confirmation requires checking the docx XML directly via `zipfile` extraction and tag counting.

content.text:
**No intra-species convention exists to preserve** — 50 of 90 multi-row runs violate levels-descending, so the ordering inside a run is capture order, not a rule. That settles the method: **a stable merge.** Runs of one species are gathered in their existing relative order, each row keeping its exact bytes and its position within its run. Nothing is re-sorted inside a species, because there is no convention there to honour, and inventing one would be a change the volume never asked for.

The sort key is element ascending, then **ionisation stage by roman value, not by string** — a string sort puts `Ca IX` before `Ca V`. Checking whether that collision is live, then building.

cd /home/claude/build && python3 - << 'EOF'
import subprocess,zipfile,shutil,re,os
subprocess.run(["pandoc","-o","/tmp/ref0.docx","--from=markdown","/dev/null"],check=True)
zin=zipfile.ZipFile("/tmp/ref0.docx")
names=zin.namelist()
data={n:zin.read(n) for n in names}
x=data["word/styles.xml"].decode("utf-8")
# (iii) theme font attrs -> literal Georgia
theme=len(re.findall(r'w:(?:ascii|hAnsi|eastAsia|cs)Theme="[^"]*"',x))
plain=len(re.findall(r'w:(?:ascii|hAnsi|eastAsia|cs)="[^"]*"',x))
x=re.sub(r'w:(ascii|hAnsi|eastAsia|cs)Theme="[^"]*"',r'w:\1="Georgia"',x)
x=re.sub(r'w:(ascii|hAnsi|eastAsia|cs)="[^"]*"',r'w:\1="Georgia"',x)
print("theme attrs converted: %d · plain attrs: %d"%(theme,plain))
# (ii) REPLACE sz in docDefaults, never insert
m=re.search(r"<w:docDefaults>.*?</w:docDefaults>",x,re.S)
dd=m.group(0)
before=re.findall(r'<w:szCs? w:val="(\d+)"\s*/>',dd)
dd2=re.sub(r'(<w:szCs? w:val=)"\d+"',r'\1"21"',dd)
x=x[:m.start()]+dd2+x[m.end():]
print("docDefaults sz values before:",before,"-> all 21")
# EntryBody style
if "EntryBody" not in x:
    style='<w:style w:type="paragraph" w:styleId="EntryBody"><w:name w:val="Entry Body"/><w:basedOn w:val="BodyText"/><w:rPr><w:i/><w:rFonts w:ascii="Georgia" w:hAnsi="Georgia"/></w:rPr></w:style>'
    x=x.replace("</w:styles>",style+"</w:styles>")
data["word/styles.xml"]=x.encode("utf-8")
# sectPr by ELEMENT NAME, not one literal serialization
doc=data["word/document.xml"].decode("utf-8")
mm=re.search(r"<w:sectPr\b[^>]*/>|<w:sectPr\b.*?</w:sectPr>",doc,re.S)
print("sectPr found by element-name anchor:",bool(mm),"| serialization:",repr(mm.group(0)[:40]) if mm else None)
sect=('<w:sectPr><w:pgSz w:w="12240" w:h="15840"/>'
      '<w:pgMar w:top="1440" w:right="1440" w:bottom="1440" w:left="1440" '
      'w:header="1440" w:footer="1440" w:gutter="0"/></w:sectPr>')
doc=doc[:mm.start()]+sect+doc[mm.end():]
data["word/document.xml"]=doc.encode("utf-8")
with zipfile.ZipFile("ref.docx","w",zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zo:
    for n in names: zo.writestr(n,data[n])
# VERIFY IN THE OBJECT
z=zipfile.ZipFile("ref.docx"); s=z.read("word/styles.xml").decode("utf-8"); d=z.read("word/document.xml").decode("utf-8")
print("--- verified in the object ---")
print("non-Georgia font attrs:",len(re.findall(r'w:(?:ascii|hAnsi|eastAsia|cs)="(?!Georgia)[^"]*"',s)))
print("remaining theme attrs :",len(re.findall(r'Theme="',s)))
print("docDefaults sz values :",re.findall(r'<w:szCs? w:val="(\d+)"',re.search(r"<w:docDefaults>.*?</w:docDefaults>",s,re.S).group(0)))
print("EntryBody present     :","EntryBody" in s)
print("pgSz / margins        :",re.search(r'w:w="12240" w:h="15840"',d) is not None, len(re.findall(r'w:(?:top|right|bottom|left|header|footer)="1440"',d)))
print("zip loads clean       :",z.testzip() is None,"| bytes:",os.path.getsize("ref.docx"))
EOF

**BUILD-31 packed and staged.** 2 + 90 = 92 members, both bundles verified against their own bytes, and the round trip proved the other way — all 92 split members compared byte-for-byte against the live tree, zero mismatches.

**Ruling 56 is recorded verbatim.** I have written it as supplying something the project has not had: an external check. Every index figure until now has been verified against other figures inside the same closed set, so a disagreement was always a tie. It no longer is — a conflict between an index and the Löwdin solution is a finding about the index.

**One thing in it I did not decide for you, and deliberately did not start.** The ruling names *the original input at the project's start* — not the absorbed Chapter 35, which has been edited through every press since. Which artefact that actually is has to be established by reading, and the ruling arrived at the handoff threshold. **So I have reversed a standing instruction: the BUILD-12 bundles are not to be retired.** They have been listed for retirement since chat 13 and never actioned, and they are the oldest surviving tree in reach — they may hold the only copy. That reversal and its reason are in §7.

**Built this chat: B7.** Spectra's channel table is now one run per species — 596 rows, 92 runs to 70, 28 elements. Both named hazards cleared on the pressed object: the He II note travelled with its seven rows, and register 1764's fault did not recur.

Two things worth your attention.

**`coords.py` had been dead for a whole build and nothing was wrong with the work that killed it.** Ruling 49 promoted Spectra's headings from level 3 to level 2 at chat 28 — built correctly, verified correctly, recorded correctly. The gate locates its sections by the literal string `### `, so two of its four checks stopped matching in the same act. No press ran at chat 29, so it surfaced only when I pressed today. The volume went on claiming its Part 0 figures are read from the companion file at build time while the instrument that makes that true could not find them. Repaired, and the rule is now a gate: a structural ruling is a silent-breakage event, and the build is not current until every gate has been re-run.

**And a method this project has leaned on since chat 8 is less sound than it looked.** Fifty-one rows across seven species appear nowhere in `pdftotext`'s output of the pressed Spectra PDF. They are present and correct in the `.docx`, so the deliverable is intact — but every "read the pressed page" check ever run here has read `pdftotext` output. It was never wrong about what it found; it was wrong about what its silence meant. Any earlier finding resting on an absence needs re-reading, and that goes to A4 as SPEC-12.

**Shortfall, named rather than left silent: B8 through B12 were not started.**

**Upload** both BUILD-31 bundles and HANDOFF-32. **Retire** the BUILD-30 bundles and HANDOFF-31 — and not the BUILD-12 bundles. The prompt for chat 31 is §8.
